head: ab2c2c02ff9aa0d62b2ee243a7a710559e0c7b8a
interpretation: Linux passed all 926 required tests and the separate tiny paused owned-QEMU provenance/cleanup mechanism. Windows compiled the production/TEST_ONLY actors but failed six new diagnostic fixture tests; all later isolated-input, PowerShell, ZIP and owned-loopback steps were skipped. The identity sidecar failed the same six tests among 344 overlapping tests; all its token/pipe/restricted/paired runtime steps were skipped.

One isolated real Python import/composition subprocess returned success, but its test compared Windows CRLF output against literal LF. Four other tests use forward-slash string suffixes for missing/close-failure injection, which do not match Windows backslash paths. These are source-supported concrete test-dispatch counterexamples, not changes to production acceptance.

The remaining parser-state test observed read_error on its first empty-object fixture, before successful parsing. The exact underlying exception was not exported; path-resolution/containment remains a source-supported candidate, not a captured runtime cause. No parser, identity or cleanup requirement is relaxed.

The original Stage0b guest run remains failed and its private report state remains unrecoverable. This short gate did not run a Windows guest or establish genuine Stage0b IPC/proxy success. No automatic retry follows this result.
